question: What is NOT a typical side effect of standard benzodiazepines?

options.A: Excessive daytime drowsiness
options.B: A rapid boost in physical energy
options.C: Dizziness and lightheadedness
options.D: Weak muscles

explanation: These medications relax the body and cause sedation rather than increasing physical energy. [learn more](BMP223_U4_T4#BMP223_U4_T4_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of fructose found in seminal vesicle fluid?

options.A: Providing energy for the sperm
options.B: Lubricating the urethra during sex
options.C: Lowering the acidity of the vagina
options.D: Killing harmful bacteria in the tract

explanation: Sperm require a lot of energy to swim, and the fructose in the seminal fluid acts as a fuel source. [learn more](BMP210_U3_T3#BMP210_U3_T3_h2)

question: How is addiction viewed in modern healthcare?

options.A: A temporary lack of personal willpower
options.B: A chronic and relapsing brain disorder
options.C: A purely physical response to heavy labor
options.D: A behavioral choice easily stopped at will

explanation: Addiction changes brain structure and function over time. It is treated as a medical condition rather than simply a matter of choice. [learn more](BMP223_U3_T8#BMP223_U3_T8_h1)

question: Why is the CA-125 blood test alone not enough to diagnose ovarian cancer?

options.A: It only measures hormone levels rather than actual tumor proteins.
options.B: It remains completely normal even when advanced tumors are present.
options.C: It changes drastically depending on the time of day the blood is drawn.
options.D: It can be high in non-cancerous conditions like fibroids or infections.

explanation: Because CA-125 rises in response to various benign inflammatory processes, it serves as a supportive marker rather than a standalone diagnostic test. [learn more](BMP320_U2_T4#BMP320_U2_T4_h3)

question: Why does a midwife compare the left limb with the right limb during an exam?

options.A: To establish a normal baseline for that specific individual
options.B: To check if the skin color matches across the entire body
options.C: To ensure the blood pressure is identical in both arms
options.D: To measure the exact height of the pregnant mother accurately

explanation: Comparing sides helps spot differences or unusual issues unique to that patient. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T1#BMP216_U3_T1_h3)

question: A laboring woman's cervical dilation graph moves to the right of the action line with severe caput and molding. What is the best interpretation?

options.A: Labor is obstructed and requires immediate senior review
options.B: Normal progress is occurring and staff should wait four hours
options.C: Contractions are too weak and require immediate oxytocin
options.D: The patient is ready to push and deliver spontaneously

explanation: Crossing the action line with signs of mechanical stress points directly to obstructed labor, demanding urgent intervention. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T2#BMP315_U1_T2_h2)

question: When does the planning phase of patient care officially begin?

options.A: When the patient is being discharged
options.B: During the evaluation of client outcomes
options.C: Right after assessment and diagnosis
options.D: Before the initial physical examination

explanation: Planning takes place once the midwife has gathered assessment data and clearly identified the client's problems or diagnoses. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T4#BMP120_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why is objective, detailed documentation essential when managing a suspected case of child maltreatment?

options.A: Detailed notes allow parents to verify the accuracy of the physical examination
options.B: Hospital management requires complete records to justify billing insurance companies
options.C: Government tax agencies audit clinical notes to determine social grant eligibility
options.D: Accurate medical records protect the child welfare and serve as legal evidence

explanation: Clear, factual descriptions of injuries and behaviors provide legally sound evidence for social welfare and legal protection proceedings. [learn more](BMP222_U4_T2#BMP222_U4_T2_h6)

question: Which primitive oral reflex helps a newborn locate the maternal nipple by turning toward a cheek stroke?

options.A: Sucking reflex
options.B: Rooting reflex
options.C: Gag reflex
options.D: Extrusion reflex

explanation: The rooting reflex makes the baby turn their head toward the side where the cheek or mouth is touched, helping them find the nipple. [learn more](BMP214_U1_T4#BMP214_U1_T4_h1)

question: How dilated must the cervix be before a craniotomy can be performed?

options.A: Firm consistency with posterior orientation
options.B: Complete dilatation
options.C: Effacement of at least 50 percent
options.D: Opening of four centimeters

explanation: The cervix must be fully dilated so that instruments can pass safely and the reduced head can be extracted without tearing the uterine tissue. [learn more](BMP311_U3_T5#BMP311_U3_T5_h3)

question: A two-year-old child falls and sustains a partial break where the bone bends and cracks on one side only. What is this called?

options.A: Greenstick fracture
options.B: Spiral fracture
options.C: Compound fracture
options.D: Transverse fracture

explanation: Children have softer, more pliable bones that tend to bend and break partially rather than snapping completely, like a fresh green tree branch. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T19#BMP111_U2_T19_h2)

question: What type of bone tissue forms the inner core of an irregular bone?

options.A: Adipose tissue
options.B: Spongy bone
options.C: Hyaline cartilage
options.D: Compact bone

explanation: The interior of irregular bones consists of spongy bone surrounded by a thin layer of compact bone. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T6#BMP111_U2_T6_h2)

question: What is the main goal of a cardiac rehabilitation program after hospital discharge?

options.A: To ensure the patient never takes any prescribed heart medications again
options.B: To replace all damaged heart valves with artificial mechanical parts
options.C: To completely reverse any existing heart muscle scar tissue back to normal
options.D: To help patients safely rebuild strength and adopt heart-healthy habits

explanation: Cardiac rehab combines supervised exercise, education, and lifestyle guidance to improve recovery and prevent future heart issues. [learn more](BMP125_U2_T4#BMP125_U2_T4_h8)

question: Which of these conditions is NOT typically linked to long-term obesity?

options.A: Type 2 diabetes
options.B: Abnormal blood fats
options.C: Iron deficiency anemia
options.D: High blood pressure

explanation: Anemia is related to iron or nutrient deficiencies, whereas diabetes, high blood pressure, and abnormal blood fats are classic weight-linked conditions. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T7#BMP118_U4_T7_h3)

question: A midwife finishes a delivery and removes her gloves safely without any tears. What should she do next?

options.A: Use an alcohol-based hand rub on gloved hands
options.B: Proceed immediately to the next patient without cleaning
options.C: Wipe hands with a dry sterile gauze pad
options.D: Wash hands thoroughly with soap and water

explanation: After removing gloves following contact with body fluids, hand hygiene is always required. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T2#BMP211_U3_T2_h3)

question: Which action happens first during a GATHER counseling session?

options.A: Explaining the management of menstrual changes
options.B: Helping the client choose a long-acting reversible method
options.C: Asking detailed questions about past obstetric history
options.D: Greeting the client warmly and ensuring privacy

explanation: The GATHER process always begins with greeting the client to build trust and set a welcoming, confidential tone. [learn more](BMP224_U2_T1#BMP224_U2_T1_h2)

question: What is the main reason for moving from a patient assessment to making a nursing diagnosis?

options.A: To discharge the patient home safely
options.B: To write down the doctor's medical prescriptions
options.C: To calculate hospital bills and bed fees
options.D: To interpret grouped data and identify patient responses

explanation: Moving from assessment to diagnosis involves analyzing the collected information to spot patterns and name the patient's actual or potential health problems. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T3#BMP120_U1_T3_h1)

question: Which complication is a major risk when a diabetic patient experiences a minor skin nick during nail grooming?

options.A: Sudden permanent loss of all fingernail growth
options.B: Instant softening of the entire nail plate
options.C: Rapid development of clubbed fingertips
options.D: Slow-healing ulcers and potential severe infection

explanation: Poor circulation and nerve damage in diabetes mean small wounds fail to heal quickly and easily turn into dangerous ulcers. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T4#BMP110_U5_T4_h5)

question: Which UNCRC article states that the best interests of the child must always come first?

options.A: Article 3
options.B: Article 12
options.C: Article 6
options.D: Article 2

explanation: Article 3 specifically mandates that the best interests of the child guide all actions taken by organizations and professionals. [learn more](BMP222_U4_T1#BMP222_U4_T1_h2)

question: Where should placentas awaiting delayed disposal be temporarily stored?

options.A: In an open bucket under the delivery bed
options.B: Inside the general staff room kitchenette
options.C: In a dedicated refrigerator separate from food and vaccines
options.D: On top of the clean linen storage trolley

explanation: Temporary cold storage prevents putrefaction, but it must be completely isolated from food or medical vaccines to avoid cross-contamination. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T5#BMP211_U3_T5_h5)

question: How do azole antifungal medications stop the growth of fungi?

options.A: By directly injecting toxic enzymes into the fungal nucleus
options.B: By dissolving the outer protein coat of fungal spores
options.C: By blocking the enzymes needed to manufacture ergosterol
options.D: By destroying the human host antibodies protecting the yeast

explanation: Azoles block the enzymes needed to make ergosterol, which weakens and stops the growth of the fungal cell membrane. [learn more](BMP124_U4_T8#BMP124_U4_T8_h2)

question: A patient walks into the antenatal clinic complaining of a severe morning headache and blurry vision. What immediate action should the midwife take?

options.A: Check the patient's blood pressure
options.B: Prescribe pain relief tablets
options.C: Send the patient home to rest
options.D: Advise the patient to drink more water

explanation: Headaches and blurry vision combined can signal dangerously high blood pressure or pre-eclampsia, requiring an immediate blood pressure check. [learn more](BMP125_U2_T2#BMP125_U2_T2_h3)

question: What is the right step when parents refuse eye ointment for their newborn?

options.A: Provide balanced counseling, obtain a signed refusal, and document it
options.B: Ignore the refusal and administer the ointment while they sleep
options.C: Threaten them with police arrest and administer the drug anyway
options.D: Discharge the mother and baby immediately without further care

explanation: Parents have a right to make decisions for their baby. If they decline after counseling, midwives respect their choice and document it properly. [learn more](BMP213_U4_T2#BMP213_U4_T2_h7)

question: Which pregnant patient has the highest medical need for regular blood thinners (anticoagulation)?

options.A: A woman with a mechanical heart valve replacement
options.B: A multiparous woman with a history of gestational diabetes
options.C: A pregnant teenager suffering from iron deficiency anemia
options.D: A primigravida experiencing mild ankle swelling at term

explanation: Mechanical heart valves have a very high risk of forming dangerous blood clots, so these patients need continuous blood thinners. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T7#BMP213_U3_T7_h2)

question: What does a distinct pause in the baby's chin movement indicate during breastfeeding?

options.A: The milk supply has completely run dry
options.B: The baby is actively swallowing milk
options.C: The infant is experiencing a mild cramp
options.D: The baby has fallen asleep at the breast

explanation: The pause in the chin corresponds to the back of the throat opening and the baby swallowing a mouthful of milk. [learn more](BMP214_U3_T2#BMP214_U3_T2_h4)

question: A client trying to conceive asks why her basal body temperature rises slightly in the second half of her cycle. What physiological explanation should the midwife give?

options.A: The developing placenta releases adrenaline to increase maternal energy.
options.B: Metabolic activity inside the maturing oocyte generates excess body heat.
options.C: Estrogen surge right before ovulation causes a temporary fever.
options.D: Progesterone released by the corpus luteum raises core body temperature.

explanation: Progesterone has a thermogenic effect on the hypothalamus, causing a measurable rise in basal body temperature following ovulation. [learn more](BMP210_U2_T4#BMP210_U2_T4_h6)

question: Why is an intravenous insulin and glucose infusion often used during labor for a diabetic mother?

options.A: To speed up cervical dilation and shorten the first stage of labor
options.B: To stop the uterus from having strong contractions
options.C: To replace the fluids lost from severe morning sickness
options.D: To keep maternal blood sugar stable and prevent low blood sugar in the newborn

explanation: Managing maternal blood sugar tightly during labor prevents the baby from having high insulin levels that cause sudden drops in newborn blood sugar after birth. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T3#BMP221_U4_T3_h7)

question: Which mild, harmless side effect often happens shortly after a patient takes misoprostol?

options.A: Sudden loss of hearing ability
options.B: Complete hair loss on the head
options.C: Shivering and mild fever
options.D: Yellow discoloration of the eyes

explanation: Temporary shivering and mild chills are common side effects of prostaglandins and usually go away on their own. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T4#BMP213_U1_T4_h6)

question: A postpartum mother has severe nipple pain and cracked skin during feeds. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: The infant has oral thrush infection
options.B: Low overall prolactin hormone levels
options.C: Inadequate maternal fluid intake
options.D: Poor attachment and shallow latch

explanation: When a baby only latches onto the nipple instead of taking a large mouthful of the areola, trauma and pain occur. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T2#BMP118_U3_T2_h4)

question: How does tall-man lettering help prevent medication errors on the ward?

options.A: It uses capital letters to highlight the differing parts of similar drug names
options.B: It automatically calculates the correct dosage for pregnant women
options.C: It ensures that only senior doctors are allowed to write dangerous drugs
options.D: It prints prescription orders in giant fonts for nurses with poor eyesight

explanation: By capitalizing specific syllables in look-alike drug names, tall-man lettering draws the eye to what makes the two medications distinct. [learn more](BMP124_U1_T2#BMP124_U1_T2_h6)

question: What is the main function of an objective checklist in an OSCE?

options.A: To score specific, step-by-step procedural actions
options.B: To replace the need for an examiner inside the room
options.C: To calculate the final grade point average of the school
options.D: To judge the student's personal mood during the exam

explanation: Checklists break down a procedure into discrete actions so examiners can mark presence or absence objectively. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T10#BMP312_U3_T10_h5)

question: By what age does a normal infant typically double their birth weight?

options.A: Twelve months
options.B: Nine months
options.C: One month
options.D: Five months

explanation: An infant's weight generally doubles by five months and triples by the end of the first year. [learn more](BMP222_U1_T1#BMP222_U1_T1_h2)

question: Which test directly looks for the actual genetic material of a virus in a sample?

options.A: Routine full blood count analysis
options.B: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate
options.C: Immunoglobulin G antibody titers
options.D: Polymerase Chain Reaction testing

explanation: PCR tests zoom in on specific viral RNA or DNA sequences, making it a very sensitive way to catch active infections. [learn more](BMP116_U4_T5#BMP116_U4_T5_h2)

question: A laboring patient who received intramuscular morphine 1 hour ago now has a respiratory rate of 10 breaths per minute and is difficult to rouse. What should the midwife do first?

options.A: Wait another hour to see if her breathing rate returns to normal on its own.
options.B: Encourage the patient to walk around the ward to shake off the sleepiness.
options.C: Call for emergency assistance and prepare the antidote and resuscitation gear.
options.D: Administer an extra dose of oral paracetamol to help with her overall comfort.

explanation: A respiratory rate under 12 breaths per minute with heavy sedation indicates opioid toxicity requiring prompt medical intervention. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T2#BMP213_U2_T2_h5)

question: What percentage of total daily energy expenditure does BMR typically account for in a sedentary adult?

options.A: Sixty to seventy-five percent
options.B: Zero to ten percent
options.C: Twenty to thirty percent
options.D: Eighty to ninety percent

explanation: BMR makes up the largest portion of daily energy use because the body's internal organs constantly require fuel just to stay alive. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T4#BMP118_U1_T4_h2)

question: Why is increased dietary fiber and fluid intake important in the care plan for hypothyroidism?

options.A: To prevent the skin from developing the thick waxy swelling of myxedema
options.B: To speed up the breakdown of fatty tissues and encourage rapid weight loss
options.C: To keep the body temperature high and prevent dangerous bouts of shivering
options.D: To help prevent and relieve the chronic constipation caused by slowed digestion

explanation: Sluggish bowel motility from a slow metabolism makes constipation common, which fiber and fluids help manage. [learn more](BMP216_U2_T6#BMP216_U2_T6_h7)

question: A pregnant woman living ten kilometers down a dirt road from the nearest clinic is due to deliver soon. Which local innovation best prevents a delay in reaching emergency care if labor complications arise?

options.A: An imported digital ultrasound machine operated by the village chief
options.B: A high-speed cargo aircraft stationed at the local primary school
options.C: A satellite television for health education in the clinic waiting room
options.D: A community-organized tricycle or motorcycle transport scheme

explanation: Local transport arrangements solve the critical first delay of reaching a health facility along poor rural roads. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T7#BMP117_U1_T7_h4)

question: Which situation is a clear example of using telemedicine?

options.A: Distributing printed health pamphlets during a community immunization drive
options.B: Performing a routine surgical procedure inside a sterile operating theater
options.C: Providing healthcare services when distance separates the provider and client
options.D: Conducting an in-person physical pelvic examination at a local clinic

explanation: Telemedicine specifically bridges geographical distance by using electronic communication tools for care delivery. [learn more](BMP123_U5_T3#BMP123_U5_T3_h2)

question: Which fetal shoulder width gets stuck behind the mother's pubic bone during shoulder dystocia?

options.A: The suboccipitobregmatic diameter
options.B: The bisacromial diameter
options.C: The menton-vertical diameter
options.D: The biparietal diameter

explanation: Shoulder dystocia happens when the baby's shoulders get stuck. The bisacromial diameter is the medical term for the width between the baby's shoulders, which gets wedged against the maternal bone. [learn more](BMP311_U1_T7#BMP311_U1_T7_h1)

question: Which of the following conditions involves high blood pressure accompanied by sudden seizures?

options.A: Gestational hypertension
options.B: Severe pre-eclampsia
options.C: Eclampsia
options.D: Chronic hypertension

explanation: Eclampsia is defined by the onset of grand mal seizures in a woman with pre-eclampsia that cannot be attributed to other neurological causes. [learn more](BMP221_U3_T7#BMP221_U3_T7_h1)

question: Why does having too many hormones often lead to sudden physical exhaustion or weight changes?

options.A: It pushes the body's metabolic rate into overdrive.
options.B: It blocks the absorption of all dietary proteins.
options.C: It causes severe retention of heavy body fluids.
options.D: It completely stops the production of digestive enzymes.

explanation: Excess metabolic hormones speed up cellular activity so fast that the body burns through energy stores much faster than usual. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T4#BMP121_U4_T4_h3)

question: Which environment places the healthcare provider on unfamiliar ground within the care recipient's personal space?

options.A: Private clinic office
options.B: Institutional theatre
options.C: Tertiary hospital ward
options.D: Community setting

explanation: In community care, the midwife visits the client's home or local territory, which changes the dynamic of control. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T5#BMP110_U2_T5_h4)

question: How should the midwife hold the baby's head while assisting the delivery of the shoulders?

options.A: With both hands placed over the parietal bones on the sides of the head
options.B: Using a pair of sterile obstetric forceps
options.C: By placing fingers directly inside the baby's mouth
options.D: By firmly grabbing the baby's neck and chin

explanation: Holding the head on the sides prevents excessive twisting of the neck and protects the cervical spine. [learn more](BMP212_U3_T2#BMP212_U3_T2_h4)

question: A pregnant woman in her first trimester complains of severe morning sickness and fatigue. Which B-vitamin is especially valuable for supporting red blood cell formation and preventing early neural tube defects?

options.A: Biotin
options.B: Niacin
options.C: Thiamine
options.D: Folate

explanation: Folate is critical during early embryonic development to build red blood cells and close the neural tube properly. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T5#BMP118_U2_T5_h3)

question: Which dietary change helps a patient waiting for surgery who has frequent gallbladder pain?

options.A: Increasing red meat intake
options.B: Avoiding all drinking water
options.C: Eating high-fat meals daily
options.D: Eating a low-fat diet

explanation: Eating less fat reduces the hormonal signals that force the gallbladder to squeeze, helping to prevent painful muscle spasms. [learn more](BMP125_U4_T5#BMP125_U4_T5_h7)

question: A teenager has had severe heavy periods ever since her very first cycle. Along with a blood count, which test is most important?

options.A: Endometrial biopsy
options.B: Hysterosalpingography
options.C: Coagulation screen
options.D: Cervical cytology smear

explanation: When heavy bleeding starts right from menarche, it often points to an underlying clotting disorder like von Willebrand disease, making a coagulation screen essential. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T3#BMP310_U3_T3_h3)

question: A newborn baby shows a strong palmar grasp on the right hand but has no response at all on the left hand after a difficult shoulder dystocia delivery. What condition does this finding most likely suggest?

options.A: General brain infection affecting both sides
options.B: Complete absence of the spinal cord
options.C: Normal variation in bilateral reflex strength
options.D: Brachial plexus injury on the left side

explanation: An asymmetric reflex following a difficult birth often points to nerve damage like a brachial plexus palsy on the weak side. [learn more](BMP214_U1_T6#BMP214_U1_T6_h5)

question: Which category includes nutrients required by the body in large daily amounts?

options.A: Micronutrients
options.B: Macronutrients
options.C: Synthetic enzymes
options.D: Trace elements

explanation: Macronutrients like carbohydrates, proteins, and fats are needed in large quantities to sustain the body. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T1#BMP118_U1_T1_h4)

question: Why must intravenous dextrose infusions be tapered down slowly rather than stopped abruptly?

options.A: To prevent the intravenous site from swelling or leaking fluids
options.B: To allow the baby's natural body temperature to rise gradually
options.C: To prevent rebound hypoglycemia caused by continued excess insulin release
options.D: To give the kidneys time to adjust to a lower fluid volume load

explanation: Stopping a high-sugar IV too fast leaves the baby with high insulin levels that consume all available blood sugar, causing a sudden drop. [learn more](BMP220_U3_T2#BMP220_U3_T2_h6)

question: How often should you check a laboring woman's temperature after her water has broken?

options.A: Every two hours
options.B: Once every shift
options.C: Every four hours
options.D: Every six hours

explanation: When membranes rupture, the risk of infection goes up. Checking the temperature every two hours helps catch any early signs of fever. [learn more](BMP212_U2_T5#BMP212_U2_T5_h1)

question: Which local food item is a particularly good and accessible source of omega-3 fatty acids for pregnant women in Nigeria?

options.A: Local oily fish like mackerel or sardine
options.B: Polished white garri from cassava
options.C: Highly refined white table sugar
options.D: Pure cornstarch mixed with water

explanation: Oily fish are rich sources of essential omega-3 fatty acids, which support fetal brain and eye development. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T3#BMP118_U2_T3_h5)

question: Why is family planning typically included in a comprehensive maternal and child health outreach package?

options.A: To support birth spacing and improve overall maternal wellbeing
options.B: To satisfy administrative paperwork requirements for donors
options.C: To replace routine immunization services entirely
options.D: To reduce the total population of children under five years

explanation: Including family planning helps women space their pregnancies safely, which lowers risks for both mothers and babies. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T3#BMP323_U1_T3_h3)

question: What is the main reason an infant is weighed with minimal clothing during a clinic visit?

options.A: To check the baby's skin for rashes
options.B: to make the baby feel cooler in hot weather
options.C: To ensure measurement accuracy
options.D: To prevent the weighing scale from rusting

explanation: Heavy clothing or diapers can falsely increase a child's weight, making accurate nutritional assessment difficult. [learn more](BMP126_U1_T4#BMP126_U1_T4_h5)

question: Why must midwives exercise caution when considering systemic antifungal medications for pregnant women?

options.A: Antifungal drugs stop breast milk production permanently after birth
options.B: Certain oral antifungals can pose risks to the developing fetus
options.C: Systemic drugs cause immediate rupture of the amniotic membranes
options.D: Fungal cells in pregnant women are completely resistant to all medications

explanation: Some systemic antifungals can harm fetal development, making safety profiles a primary consideration during pregnancy. [learn more](BMP116_U3_T1#BMP116_U3_T1_h7)

question: What does the acceptance stage of grief mean for a bereaved individual?

options.A: Coming to terms with reality and learning to live with the loss
options.B: Completing all five stages within twenty-four hours
options.C: Being completely joyful about the tragedy
options.D: Forgetting that the event took place

explanation: Acceptance is about acknowledging the new reality and finding a way forward, not about being happy. [learn more](BMP120_U5_T3#BMP120_U5_T3_h6)

question: Which harmful practice do some mothers mistakenly try when their child develops acute watery diarrhea?

options.A: Giving frequent small sips of ORS from a clean cup
options.B: Continuing to breastfeed the infant on demand
options.C: Giving the correct dose of zinc tablets daily
options.D: Withholding food to let the child's stomach rest

explanation: Starving a sick child is a dangerous misconception that worsens nutritional status and delays gut healing. [learn more](BMP222_U3_T3#BMP222_U3_T3_h6)

question: A midwife at a primary health centre wants to check on a breastfeeding mother who was discharged yesterday without making a physical home visit. What is the best digital approach?

options.A: Send a printed pamphlet through the mail system
options.B: Cancel all follow-up care until complications arise
options.C: Conduct a video call to observe latching and maternal recovery
options.D: Wait until the child turns one year old for a check

explanation: A video call allows visual assessment of feeding and healing without requiring travel. [learn more](BMP123_U4_T4#BMP123_U4_T4_h3)

question: What time frame defines a surgical site infection after an operation?

options.A: Only while the patient is sleeping
options.B: Within 12 hours of the surgery
options.C: Up to 30 days post-operative
options.D: After exactly six months of healing

explanation: An infection is classified as a surgical site infection if it develops around the incision within thirty days after the procedure. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T3#BMP116_U5_T3_h2)

question: Which specific structures form the joint at the back of the thorax called the costotransverse joint?

options.A: The rib head and the intervertebral disc
options.B: The sternal angle and the costal cartilage
options.C: The xiphoid process and the seventh rib
options.D: The rib tubercle and the vertebral transverse process

explanation: The costotransverse joint connects the bony bump on the rib to the side projection of the corresponding spine bone. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T9#BMP111_U2_T9_h4)

question: What dangerous habit must midwives avoid when handling used hypodermic needles?

options.A: Carrying them on a kidney dish to the disposal point
options.B: Using a single-handed scoop technique if recapping is required
options.C: Dropping them directly into a nearby puncture-resistant box
options.D: Recapping needles using a traditional two-handed method

explanation: Two-handed recapping is a primary cause of accidental needle-stick injuries because the hand holding the cap is directly in the path of the needle point. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T4#BMP116_U5_T4_h4)

question: Which type of immunity is transferred naturally from a mother to her baby across the placenta?

options.A: Innate immunity
options.B: Active immunity
options.C: Passive immunity
options.D: Herd immunity

explanation: Maternal antibodies cross the placenta to provide temporary protection to the newborn, which is a classic form of passive immunity. [learn more](BMP117_U3_T3#BMP117_U3_T3_h2)

question: Why are midwives well-positioned to promote mental health in women?

options.A: They have frequent contact with women throughout pregnancy and childbirth
options.B: They manage patients exclusively inside large psychiatric hospitals
options.C: They are the only healthcare workers allowed to give psychiatric drugs
options.D: They receive specialized training in neurosurgery and brain chemistry
